transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Gomez (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (Latitude CTO), Rhea Kapoor (ML Engineer), Tom Wallace (Security)

Summary:
Quick hosted API walkthrough focusing on chat/text generation basics: streaming responses, request parameters (temperature, max_tokens, system/user messages), retry/backoff behavior, and pricing/latency tradeoffs. Customer interested in a short pilot comparing latency and cost vs their current OpenAI setup and wants security docs (SOC2, KMS/enterprise key options).

Topics:
- Streaming responses and SDK usage
- Prompt/parameter guidance
- Retry and idempotency patterns
- Latency and cost tradeoffs (batching vs single token latency)
- Security/compliance (SSO, SOC2, KMS)

Transcript:
00:00 Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is samir from redwood, i'm joined by elena from our se team.
00:12 Mark: hey, hi thanks, mark here, rhea and tom are also on, thanks for doing this.
00:18 Elena: great — we'll do a quick 30 min demo and then leave time for q's and pilot discussion, hope that works.
00:27 Rhea: sounds good, we have about 40 minutes so good cadence.
00:33 Samir: quick agenda, hosted api, chat/text basics, streaming, params, retries and then pricing/next steps. i'll share a deck link in the chat, and elena will do a quick live demo of the console and SDK.
00:48 Samir: link: https://redwood.example/deck/hosted-api-chat (note: link placeholder)
00:55 Elena: okay i'm sharing screen, starting with the console — model selector, streaming toggle, and the request inspector.
01:20 Elena: here you can see the streaming option, when enabled it starts sending partial tokens as they arrive, reduces perceived latency for users. in node/python we provide a streaming sdk example — i will share github snippet after.
01:45 Rhea: quick q — does streaming increase cost? like are we billed per partial chunk or only final tokens?
01:55 Elena: billed per token generated, streaming doesn't duplicate billing. you still pay per output token and any input tokens. small transcription note: sometimes ppl expect chunk billing but it's per-token.
02:14 Tom: security question — can you use our KMS, we need to use customer-managed keys and logs forward to our SIEM.
02:24 Samir: yes, private deployments support customer-managed KMS; for hosted we have integrations for enterprise customers and can offer bring-your-own-key options or dedicated key wrapping — we'll share the security packet. also, audit logs can be forwarded to their syslog/SIEM.
02:45 Mark: do you have SOC2 and iso certs, and how does data retention work for hosted?
02:52 Samir: we are SOC2 compliant, standard enterprise package includes configurable data retention and option to disable retention for logs; i'll share the certs and the security whitepaper.
03:10 Elena: back to streaming: demo — sending a chat message, set system prompt, user prompt, temperature .2, max_tokens 256, streaming on. watch response come in token by token.
03:30 Elena: (typing) the stream shows partials every ~100ms in this demo, your app can render partials, then finalizes once generation completes. note: network jitter can affect chunk boundaries.
03:52 Rhea: what about retries? if connection drops during stream, do you resume or restart?
04:02 Elena: currently the hosted api supports retry with idempotency keys for non-streaming; for streaming we recommend client-side reconnect + re-request with same conversation context — we provide a resumable pattern in the SDK using message ids and last_token_index. small caveat: resumability depends on short lived kv cache, if older than policy then it falls back to re-generation.
04:35 Mark: hmm that sounds ok — we need clear guarantees for partial resume, especially for web chat flows.
04:42 Elena: agreed, for strict resume you can use our conversation state API or send prior messages as context. we'll share example code.
05:00 Samir: about parameters — common patterns: temperature 0-1 (0.0 deterministic), top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty. we recommend low temp for deterministic assistant tasks and higher for creative copy.
05:24 Rhea: and token limits, sequence lengths — we use long contexts up to 16k — how do you handle kv cache and latency?
05:35 Elena: runtime uses kv cache and selective kernel choices; longer context increases compute per token and memory, we have model variants optimized for long context. for latency, prefix caching can help — we do automatic prefix caching for repeated system prompts.
05:58 Tom: okay slightly off topic — what's your multi-region routing? we need EU data residency for customers.
06:10 Samir: hosted api supports region routing, you can pin requests to eu-west region, and for regulated workloads we recommend Private deployment, but many customers use hosted eu regions for residency.
06:28 Mark: cost question — how do you price streaming vs non streaming? do you have per-token and per-embedding units?
06:37 Samir: pricing is per-token for generation + per-input tokens + separate embedding pricing. streaming doesn't change unit cost. we have committed use discounts for Dedicated/Reserved.
06:51 Rhea: any examples on batching? our product does many short requests and we want to optimize tokens and throughput.
07:00 Elena: batching reduces cost but increases latency — batch windowing is configurable on Dedicated; hosted has auto-batching heuristics that try to keep latency SLO while batching. we can share a cost/latency tradeoff chart — will add to benchmark spreadsheet.
07:24 Mark: can we run a short pilot to compare latency vs our current OpenAI endpoint? want to measure median p95 latencies and cost per 1M tokens.
07:35 Samir: yes pilot is common — we usually run 1-2 week pilot with a small reserved throughput, we run benchmarks and produce a report. elena will share the benchmark spreadsheet and scripts.
07:50 Elena: note on retries/backoff: we use standard exponential backoff with jitter. for idempotent calls send idempotency-header to avoid double charge on retries for non-streaming. streaming reconnects should re-run with conversation state.
08:15 Rhea: do you have SDKs for mobile (iOS/Android) streaming?
08:23 Elena: we have JS/Node and Python streaming libraries, mobile customers often use websocket-based client that connects to our edge gateway; we can share a mobile integration guide.
08:40 Mark: any hard SLOs on latency? p95 numbers?
08:46 Elena: for our hosted catalog models we publish median/p95 profiles on the model page; typical p95 for small/medium seq is X ms in our nearest region — i'll include the public perf page link. (note: placeholder numbers omitted in transcript due to quick demo)
09:05 Tom: for compliance we need to ensure RBAC and SSO, can you integrate with our Okta and provide audit trails per user?
09:15 Samir: yes SAML/Okta is supported, RBAC roles via the console, and full audit trails are available in the enterprise package.
09:30 Rhea: fine — on the SDK example you mentioned resume tokens, will that work if connection dies after 80% of tokens?
09:38 Elena: it depends, we store a per-request token index in the cache; resume is best-effort for short windows. generally for chat we record message ids and re-emit the last message + partial to continue.
09:58 Mark: any gotchas for streaming with long contexts? like memory blowups?
10:06 Elena: just monitoring of kv cache size and sequence length. we recommend trimming history or using embedding-based retrieval for very long histories.
10:20 Samir: quick recap of pilot scope: customer provides sample prompts and SLOs, we run benchmark comparing p50/p95 and cost, share report. pilot will include streaming + non-streaming tests.
10:40 Mark: ok next question — support for function/tool calling? we want structured outputs sometimes.
10:48 Elena: yes we support structured output and function calling; console shows call schema and we can validate responses.
11:05 Rhea: awesome. any limits on concurrent streams per account?
11:11 Samir: there are soft limits that we can raise per account; for high concurrency we recommend Dedicated pools.
11:25 Tom: last sec — please send us the SOC2 and network diagram and the KMS integration doc.
11:32 Samir: will do, i'll include them in the follow-up email along with the pricing and pilot steps.
11:40 Elena: i'll share the benchmark templates and streaming sdk samples after the call.
11:50 Mark: thanks all, this was helpful.
11:53 Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule pilot planning.
12:00 (call end)
